The Egyptian taskmasters are shown striking Hebrew slaves in their labors ('וַיַּרְא בְּסִבְלֹתָם' - 'and he saw their burdens'), establishing the Egyptian leadership as perpetrators of oppression. Moses's action against the Egyptian overseer, and his subsequent flight from Pharaoh's wrath, frame the authority structure (Pharaoh and his agents) as the wrongdoers. The Hebrew people are portrayed as victims of unjust labor, not as being in the wrong. Moses's defensive intervention on behalf of the oppressed further reinforces that the leadership apparatus is unjust.
